Refinements checked nothing: `let bad: Sample = 1.5` compiled, and SYNTAX's
own E_RefinementRejected example was false against the binary. Two roots.

(1) parse_let DISCARDED the `: T` annotation (`let (_, p_ty) = ...`), so a
let-binding never reached any refinement check. LetStmt now carries the
annotation as a third node arg (the NTypeAnn, mirroring FnStmt's ret_ann);
the ~19 LetStmt sites across parser/infer/lower move in lockstep. The
absent-annotation sentinel REUSES the value node rather than minting a fresh
LitUnit, so the handle counter is unshifted and the emit is byte-identical
(m2 == m3, not a 148k renumbering transition).

operands are node handles) resolved via node_const to None -> V_Pending.
subst_self(pred, value_handle) swaps the self-operand for the value node at
infer_pat, where the value handle lives; apply_refinement_constraint peels
the transparent alias and verify discharges the substituted predicate.

mentl/73a71e0:
Add §5.O — the O(1) architecture. The only acceptable complexity for any
operation is O(1), because the kernel's only native access is the O(1)
flat-array handle chase, so a super-constant op re-derives what an edge already
connects: "O(1) only" is the Carried-Truth Law read at the performance scale
(Law 1 gains this corollary). The 8-agent diagnosis of the ~23-min self-compile
(env_find_flat O(n^2), dedup, esc O(n^2), instantiate clone, the 4GB never-free
amplifier, zero parallelism) all reduce to one class — the compiler re-derives
by name what a handle already connects. The unifying fix is names-are-handles,
built in four layers: handle-interning substrate, O(1) reads (env/dedup/
find_mapping/esc), per-decl arena (ownership drop), parallel cursors
(deterministic handle partition), each with its self-hosting verdict.

O(1) frontier. Mark landed what was described as open: the crown soundness gate

noodles/738d131:
Morgan wants it off the browser and onto the phone. The app was already
most of the way there without knowing it: zero external requests (Tone is
bundled, no fonts, no CDNs), everything client-side, and the whole thing
including the drum bank is under a megabyte — so 'works offline' is a
manifest and a service worker away, not an architecture change.

vite-plugin-pwa generates both. display:standalone drops the browser
chrome but keeps the status bar (on a couch you still want the clock).
Workbox precaches all 28 files, the 16 WAVs included: without the sample
bank the drums fall back to the synth kit and it isn't the same
instrument. registerType:autoUpdate keeps installed clients current on
next launch, silently — no update nags, same as the app's no-push ethos.

The icon is the product's own UI: four rounded clips in the four track
colors on the app's dark tile, generated by scripts/make-icons.mjs into
public/icons (192, 512, 512-maskable padded into the safe zone, and a
180 apple-touch-icon since iOS ignores the manifest for home screens).
Install itself stays pull-only — the browser menu has it, and the ? page
grows an 'install' row only when Chrome says the app qualifies and isn't
installed yet.

Receipts: .tmp/dbg-pwa.mjs installs the worker, waits out the precache,
cuts the network (proving it dead with a failing cache-busting fetch —
navigator.onLine lies under CDP), reloads, and asserts the app boots,
all 16 samples are cache-served, a dice roll lands, and it plays; smoke
now asserts the worker registers and the manifest links on every run.
